cards.title: THE HALL CLOSET
cards.tagline: FIVE SHELVES OF EVERYTHING THAT HAD NOWHERE ELSE TO GO.
cards.objective: The hall closet is where everything that had to go somewhere ended up. This card is the map and the order.
cards.start_here: HCZ-001 Linen Shelf Zone. Empty one shelf onto the hallway floor before you touch anything else. A closet this deep cannot be sorted in place; you have to see the back wall to know what you own.
how_to_play: 1. Deal the five ZONE cards face up. Pick the one that is annoying you today, or take the one this card says to start at.
2. Lay out that zone's three FRICTION cards. Keep the ones that are true in your closet. Put the rest back.
3. Turn a friction card over and pick the answer that is true. It names a ROOT CAUSE.
4. The root cause card names the ACTION cards that fix that cause. Pick the one that matches the time you actually have: fifteen or thirty minutes.
5. Do it standing up, with the card in your hand.
6. Read the victory condition out loud. If it is not true yet, you are not finished, and that is the whole scoring system.
7. Fill in the zone's STANDARD card with a pen and put it where the zone is.
8. Draw an EVENT card when an ordinary hard day happens, and see whether the standard held.
cards.players: 1 to 6. With more than one, deal the friction cards out and let each person keep the ones they believe. Disagreement is the useful part, not a problem to resolve before starting.
cards.six_s: Sort, Straighten, Shine, Safety, Standardize, Sustain
cards.safety_first: Do HCA-011 The Full Closet Safety And Height Walk before any rebuild. It takes thirty minutes and covers every shelf's height, the stool, and whether bleach and ammonia are kept apart.

cards.title: LINEN SHELF ZONE
cards.tagline: THREE SETS PER BED. ONE PILLOWCASE EACH. THE SIZE ON THE EDGE.
cards.objective: Holds the sheets, towels, and blankets the beds in this house actually rotate through.
callouts: Sheet sets nested inside their own matching pillowcases
A bed-size label fixed to the shelf edge under each stack
A stack of folded everyday towels no taller than a forearm
Two spare blankets standing on the top shelf
Clear space above the blankets with nothing stacked on them
Queen and king sets sitting on a lower shelf than the guest blankets
cards.done_looks_like: Three sheet sets per bed, each nested inside one of its own pillowcases, with the bed size written on the shelf edge underneath. Everyday towels folded to one width in a stack no taller than your forearm. Two spare blankets on the top shelf with nothing balanced on them.

safety_checks.question: Fall
safety_checks.text: Pulling a towel from the bottom of a chest-high stack brings the whole pile down onto your face and the hallway floor.

safety_checks.question: Fall, cut, or crush
safety_checks.text: Damp-weight blankets and a full shelf of folded cotton are heavier than they look; check the shelf brackets are screwed into studs, not just into plasterboard.

the_call.title: The good set you never put on a bed
the_call.text: There is a sheet set here that is too nice to use and too nice to give away, so it has sat at the front of the shelf for years while you sleep on the worn ones. Settle it with a date: put it on a bed this month, or accept that it is a keepsake rather than a linen. Keepsakes can live in a memory box. They cannot live on the shelf you reach into every week.

cards.title: CLEANING EQUIPMENT ZONE
cards.tagline: EVERYTHING HANGS. NOTHING TOUCHES THE FLOOR. THE DOOR SWINGS CLEAR.
cards.objective: Parks the vacuum, broom, and mop so they come out in one motion and go back without a fight.
callouts: A vacuum standing inside a taped floor outline
Its cord wrapped neatly around the body
A zipped bag of attachments clipped to the vacuum's handle
A broom hanging handle-down from a wall clip, head clear of the floor
A mop and a duster hanging the same way, heads clear of the floor
The closet door swinging fully open without touching anything
cards.done_looks_like: The vacuum standing inside a taped floor outline with its cord wrapped and every crevice tool and brush head zipped in one bag clipped to its handle. Broom, mop, and duster hanging handle-down from wall clips with the heads clear of the floor. The closet door swinging fully open without touching anything.

safety_checks.question: Fall, cut, or crush
safety_checks.text: Unclipped handles slide down the wall and drop across the doorway or onto whoever opens the door.

safety_checks.question: Water and electricity
safety_checks.text: A damp mop head or a wet bucket stored against a vacuum cord in a closed closet is the one combination to refuse; check the cord for cracked insulation near the plug while you have it out.

the_call.title: The vacuum you keep meaning to fix
the_call.text: It has a split hose or a dead brush roll, and it sits here because throwing out a machine that mostly works feels wasteful. Give it a repair date written on masking tape stuck to the body. If that date passes and you have not ordered the part, you have your answer: the repair was never going to happen, and the broken machine has been standing where the working one needs to stand. Recycle it and keep the one that runs.

cards.title: CLEANING SUPPLY ZONE
cards.tagline: ONE CADDY PER ROOM. BLEACH AND AMMONIA APART. OUT OF SMALL HANDS.
cards.objective: Holds the products you clean with, grouped so you carry the right handful to the right room.
callouts: Two or three caddies, each labeled with the room it serves

Gloves and cloths riding inside each caddy
cards.done_looks_like: Two or three caddies, each labeled on the end with the room it serves, every bottle wearing its original label, bleach products and ammonia products on separate shelves, and the whole zone up out of a small child's reach or behind a latch.

safety_checks.question: Poison, choke, or strangle
safety_checks.text: Bleach stored beside an ammonia glass cleaner, and any product in an unlabeled bottle at a height a child can reach from the hallway floor.

safety_checks.question: Burn or fire
safety_checks.text: Aerosol tins and solvent-based sprays sitting against a closet wall that backs onto a boiler or a hot water pipe; move them to the coolest shelf.

the_call.title: Eleven bottles, each a third full
the_call.text: You buy a new one because you cannot see what is left in the old one, and the shelf now carries four glass cleaners, three floor sprays, and a scatter of part-used others. The rule that settles it: one open bottle per job. Pour identical products together, and for the rest, accept that finishing a half bottle down the drain costs you a little while keeping it costs you the shelf you need. You did not save money by keeping them. You paid twice and stored the evidence.

safety_checks.question: Poison, choke, or strangle
safety_checks.text: Button cells and loose AAAs rolling to the closet floor where a small child finds them at eye level.

safety_checks.question: Fall, cut, or crush
safety_checks.text: A shrink-wrapped bulk pack of paper towel stored above head height slides free the moment you tug the corner of it.

the_call.title: The offer that made you buy twelve
the_call.text: Bulk buying feels thrifty right up to the point where a warehouse pack blocks the shelf and you buy more anyway because you cannot see past it. Set your maximum as the number that fits inside the bin without stacking above the rim, then hold it: if a deal will not fit the bin, the deal is not for you. And date each pack with a marker as it arrives, pulling the oldest first. Undated bulk is where the saving quietly expires.

safety_checks.question: Fall
safety_checks.text: Reaching for a top-shelf bin while balanced on a hallway chair, with a lid you cannot see over hiding the step down.

safety_checks.question: Fall, cut, or crush
safety_checks.text: A bin of decorations lifted down overhead shifts its weight halfway and lands on your foot or on whoever is holding the door.

the_call.title: The bin you have moved three times without opening
the_call.text: It has survived a house move and two closet reshuffles, and you still cannot say what is in it. That is the decision you have been avoiding, and the avoidance is itself the answer. Open it on the floor today. For each thing inside, name the specific occasion in the next twelve months when you will use it: a birthday, a holiday, a trip already booked. Anything you cannot name an occasion for does not get the lid back on, because a sealed bin of unknowns is not storage, it is a decision you agreed to keep paying for.

cards.confirm_in_30_seconds: Count what you used in the past month. If the honest number is a third of what is stored here, the space is not too small.
cards.instruction: This is a Sort problem. Draw one of the action cards listed and do it now, at the length you actually have.

art.subject: a cleaning supply shelf crowded with far more partly-used bottles than a single job would ever need
must_show: More things are kept here than the zone's job needs.
art.accept_test: One idea, one object, no room tour. If the picture could illustrate three different causes it is rejected.

cards.title: NO ASSIGNED HOME
cards.objective: The thing has no single defined destination, so it lands wherever the hand opens.
cards.confirm_in_30_seconds: Ask where one specific item lives. If two people answer differently, or nobody answers, it has no home.
cards.instruction: This is a Straighten problem. Draw one of the action cards listed and do it now, at the length you actually have.

art.accept_test: One idea, one object, no room tour. If the picture could illustrate three different causes it is rejected.

cards.title: POOR VISIBILITY
cards.objective: You own it, but you cannot see it, so you buy it again or forget it.
cards.confirm_in_30_seconds: Open the door and, without moving anything, name what is at the back. If you cannot, that stock is invisible.
cards.instruction: This is a Straighten problem. Draw one of the action cards listed and do it now, at the length you actually have.

art.subject: a sealed opaque storage bin on a closet shelf giving no hint of what is inside it
must_show: You own it, but you cannot see it, so you buy it again or forget it.
art.accept_test: One idea, one object, no room tour. If the picture could illustrate three different causes it is rejected.

cards.title: POOR ACCESSIBILITY
cards.objective: The people who use it cannot reach it safely, or at all.
cards.confirm_in_30_seconds: Have the shortest person who uses this zone fetch what they need daily. If they climb, reach overhead, or ask for help, the height is wrong.
cards.instruction: This is a Safety problem. Draw one of the action cards listed and do it now, at the length you actually have.

art.subject: a hallway chair standing in for a step stool beneath a high closet shelf, no stool anywhere in the closet itself
must_show: The people who use it cannot reach it safely, or at all.
art.accept_test: One idea, one object, no room tour. If the picture could illustrate three different causes it is rejected.

cards.title: INSUFFICIENT CAPACITY
cards.objective: The right storage exists and genuinely cannot hold what belongs in it.
cards.confirm_in_30_seconds: Put back only what belongs here. If it still will not close, or still stacks four deep, the capacity is the problem, not the habit.
cards.instruction: This is a Sort problem. Draw one of the action cards listed and do it now, at the length you actually have.

art.accept_test: One idea, one object, no room tour. If the picture could illustrate three different causes it is rejected.

cards.title: MISSING STANDARD
cards.objective: Nobody agreed what good looks like, so everybody is right.
cards.confirm_in_30_seconds: Ask two people in the house to describe this zone when it is finished. Two different answers means there is no standard to keep.
cards.instruction: This is a Standardize problem. Draw one of the action cards listed and do it now, at the length you actually have.

art.subject: a bare shelf edge in a closet with no dated card or count marker anywhere on it

art.accept_test: One idea, one object, no room tour. If the picture could illustrate three different causes it is rejected.

cards.title: MISSING TRIGGER
cards.objective: The reset is a good intention with nothing to attach it to.
cards.confirm_in_30_seconds: Name the moment it happens. If the answer is "when I get round to it", there is no trigger and it will not survive a bad week.
cards.instruction: This is a Sustain problem. Draw one of the action cards listed and do it now, at the length you actually have.

art.subject: a vacuum with a split hose standing untouched in a closet corner, no repair date marked anywhere on it

cards.title: SAFETY CONSTRAINT
cards.objective: The current arrangement can hurt somebody, and that outranks tidy.
cards.confirm_in_30_seconds: Look for the four: a blade your hand would meet, weight above shoulder height, heat beside something that burns, and an unsafe placement near a child's reach.

cards.title: POOR REPLENISHMENT
cards.objective: Consumables run out unnoticed, and stock ages out of use unseen.
cards.confirm_in_30_seconds: Find the last one of something you use daily. If nothing tells you it is the last one, you will find out at the worst possible moment.
cards.instruction: This is a Standardize problem. Draw one of the action cards listed and do it now, at the length you actually have.

art.accept_test: One idea, one object, no room tour. If the picture could illustrate three different causes it is rejected.

cards.title: CONFLICTING USERS
cards.objective: Two people run one zone by two designs, so it is permanently half of each.
cards.confirm_in_30_seconds: Do the shared task together, once. The argument that starts is the conflict, and it is a design problem, not a character problem.

cards.title: UNCLEAR OWNERSHIP
cards.objective: Nobody specific is responsible for resetting this zone, so upkeep depends on whoever notices first.
cards.confirm_in_30_seconds: Ask who resets this zone. If the honest answer is "whoever gets to it" or two names with no agreement, there is no owner.
cards.instruction: This is a Sustain problem. Draw one of the action cards listed and do it now, at the length you actually have.

art.subject: an unrefilled bin sitting on a closet shelf at the end of the day, no single person's name attached to it

cards.title: SENTIMENTAL ATTACHMENT
cards.objective: The item is kept for what it represents, not because it is used, and the guilt stalls Sort indefinitely.
cards.confirm_in_30_seconds: Ask if you would buy this again today for what it does. If the answer is no but you still cannot decide, the hold is sentimental.
cards.instruction: This is a Sort problem. Draw one of the action cards listed and do it now, at the length you actually have.

art.subject: a noticeably nicer sheet set sitting untouched at the front of a linen shelf, visibly never used

cards.title: UNRESOLVED DECISION
cards.objective: The item is not clutter, it is a decision that has not been made, so it is stacked instead of acted on.
cards.confirm_in_30_seconds: Pick up one piece. If your first thought is a verb (pay, sign, call, decide) rather than a place, it needs a decision, not a home.
cards.instruction: This is a Sort problem. Draw one of the action cards listed and do it now, at the length you actually have.

art.subject: a sealed, undated storage bin sitting on a closet shelf that has clearly been moved more than once without ever being opened
must_show: The item is not clutter, it is a decision that has not been made, so it is stacked instead of acted on.

cards.title: PERCEPTUAL BLINDNESS
cards.objective: The clutter has been visible so long the eye stops flagging it as a problem.
cards.confirm_in_30_seconds: Ask someone who does not live here to name what looks out of place. If they see it instantly and you had stopped noticing, this is the cause.
cards.instruction: This is a Sort problem. Draw one of the action cards listed and do it now, at the length you actually have.

art.subject: a vacuum with a split hose standing so long in its closet corner that it now blends in among the working equipment around it
must_show: The clutter has been visible so long the eye stops flagging it as a problem.
art.accept_test: One idea, one object, no room tour. If the picture could illustrate three different causes it is rejected.

cards.title: CLEAR THE SHELF AND CHECK EVERY SET
cards.objective: Unfold every set and check it is complete and fits a bed you still own, so nothing half-usable survives on a technicality.
cards.why_it_matters: A set with a missing half or slack elastic only reveals itself at three in the morning, the worst possible time to find out.
steps: Unfold every set and check it is complete and fits a bed you still own. The flat sheet whose fitted half vanished, fitted sheets with slack elastic that pop off a corner at three in the morning, and towels that smell sour an hour after drying all leave.
Set aside anything still good but unlikely to get used, to give away rather than bin.
Re-nest each surviving set inside its own matching pillowcase before it goes back.
cards.victory_condition: Every set on the shelf is complete, fits a bed you still own, and no towel carries a sour smell.

art.subject: a linen shelf mid-clear with a matched set half-nested into its own pillowcase, a bin bag sitting on the floor beside it
must_show: Every set on the shelf is complete, fits a bed you still own, and no towel carries a sour smell.
art.accept_test: The picture shows the finished state the victory condition describes, not the work in progress and not a person doing it.

cards.title: LABEL EVERY STACK AND SET THE HEIGHT LIMIT
cards.objective: Write each bed size on the shelf edge under its stack, and keep every stack no taller than a forearm.
cards.why_it_matters: A label-less stack forces a guess at bedtime, and a stack taller than a forearm is a fall waiting on the next towel pulled from the bottom.
steps: Group sets by the bed they fit, queen and king low, guest blankets on top.
Write the bed size and set count on the shelf edge under each stack.
Split any stack taller than a forearm into two shorter ones.
cards.victory_condition: Every stack is labeled with its bed size, and no stack stands taller than a forearm.
cards.source: hand authored, steps grounded in the Manual passes

art.subject: a hand marking a bed size onto a shelf-edge label under a folded linen stack no taller than a forearm
must_show: Every stack is labeled with its bed size, and no stack stands taller than a forearm.
art.accept_test: The picture shows the finished state the victory condition describes, not the work in progress and not a person doing it.

cards.title: STAND EVERY HANDLE UP AND CHECK THE WORKING END
cards.objective: Stand every handle up and look at the working end, so nothing kept only for parts survives another season.
cards.why_it_matters: A splayed broom pushes dust instead of gathering it, and a vacuum kept for parts never harvested is just standing where the working one needs to stand.
steps: Stand every handle up and look at the working end. Brooms with splayed bristles that push dust rather than gather it, the mop head that no longer twists off its plate, and the old vacuum you keep for parts you have never once harvested all go out this week.
Wrap any surviving cord neatly and zip loose attachments into one bag.
Recycle anything that goes, and note the repair each surviving tool actually needs.
cards.victory_condition: Every remaining tool has a working end, and nothing is being kept for parts that were never actually used.

art.subject: a hand standing a broom up to check its bristles, a splayed broom set apart on the floor beside a bin bag
must_show: Every remaining tool has a working end, and nothing is being kept for parts that were never actually used.
art.accept_test: The picture shows the finished state the victory condition describes, not the work in progress and not a person doing it.

cards.title: HANG EVERY HANDLE AND TAPE THE VACUUM'S SPOT
cards.objective: Fit a rail so every handle hangs bristles-up, and tape a floor outline for the vacuum with a repair date on anything still broken.
cards.why_it_matters: A handle left standing on the floor bends and re-soils what you just cleaned, and a repair with no date attached never actually happens.
inputs: masking tape and a marker for the repair date
steps: Fit a rail or clips at a height that clears the floor, and hang every handle bristles or mop-head up.
Tape a floor outline for the vacuum and park it there after every use.
If anything still needs a repair, write the date on masking tape stuck to the body.
cards.victory_condition: Every handle hangs clear of the floor, the vacuum parks inside its taped outline, and any repair still needed carries a written date.
cards.source: hand authored, steps grounded in the Manual passes

art.subject: a broom, mop and duster hanging handle-down from wall clips above a taped floor outline holding a parked vacuum
must_show: Every handle hangs clear of the floor, the vacuum parks inside its taped outline, and any repair still needed carries a written date.
art.accept_test: The picture shows the finished state the victory condition describes, not the work in progress and not a person doing it.

cards.title: LINE UP EVERY BOTTLE AND DISPOSE OF THE UNMARKED
cards.objective: Line every bottle up on the hallway floor and only pour identical products together, so nothing unmarked survives unidentified.
cards.why_it_matters: A decanted, unmarked bottle is a real hazard the moment somebody other than you reaches for it.
steps: Line every bottle up on the hallway floor. Anything decanted into an unmarked spray bottle gets disposed of according to its own instructions, and the specialty cleaner bought for one stain years ago goes with it. Only identical products get poured together.
Group only identical products together before anything goes back.
Set aside anything unlabeled for safe disposal per its own instructions.
cards.victory_condition: Every bottle on the shelf is in its own original, labeled container, and no two different products have been mixed.

art.subject: a row of cleaning bottles lined up on a hallway floor, each one wearing its own original label
must_show: Every bottle on the shelf is in its own original, labeled container, and no two different products have been mixed.
art.accept_test: The picture shows the finished state the victory condition describes, not the work in progress and not a person doing it.

cards.title: BUILD TWO CADDIES AND SEPARATE BLEACH FROM AMMONIA
cards.objective: Build a bathroom caddy and a kitchen caddy, and move bleach and ammonia products onto separate shelves out of a child's reach.
cards.why_it_matters: Bleach and ammonia stored together is a real hazard, and a caddy per room means carrying the whole job in one hand instead of walking back twice.
steps: Sort bleach products onto one shelf and ammonia products onto a separate one.
Build a bathroom caddy and a kitchen caddy, gloves and cloths riding inside each.
Move the whole zone up out of a small child's reach, or fit a latch.
cards.victory_condition: Bleach and ammonia sit on separate shelves, two labeled caddies exist, and the zone sits out of a small child's reach.
cards.source: hand authored, steps grounded in the Manual passes

art.subject: two labeled cleaning caddies, one marked for the bathroom and one for the kitchen, standing on separate shelves from a row of bleach bottles
must_show: Bleach and ammonia sit on separate shelves, two labeled caddies exist, and the zone sits out of a small child's reach.
art.accept_test: The picture shows the finished state the victory condition describes, not the work in progress and not a person doing it.

cards.title: TAKE THE LOT OUT AND CHECK EVERY PACK
cards.objective: Take the lot out and check every battery, bulb and bulk pack, so nothing unusable keeps its shelf space.
cards.why_it_matters: A battery you cannot vouch for and a bulb for a fitting you no longer own are both taking up space a real reserve needs.
steps: Take the lot out. Loose batteries you cannot vouch for, bulbs for fittings you replaced when you went over to LED, and the bulk paper towel pack too big to lift down alone all leave now.
Recycle any pack for a fitting the house no longer uses.
Set the bulk paper towel pack down at waist height, not overhead.
cards.victory_condition: Every battery is in its original pack, every bulb fits a fitting the house still uses, and nothing on the shelf is too heavy to lift down alone.

art.subject: a backstock shelf cleared onto the floor, loose batteries set apart from bulb packs still in their original boxes
must_show: Every battery is in its original pack, every bulb fits a fitting the house still uses, and nothing on the shelf is too heavy to lift down alone.
art.accept_test: The picture shows the finished state the victory condition describes, not the work in progress and not a person doing it.

cards.title: SET A MINIMUM AND MAXIMUM ON EVERY BIN
cards.objective: Write a minimum and maximum on the shelf edge for toilet roll, bulbs and batteries, and date every pack as it arrives.
cards.why_it_matters: A shelf with no written limit is where an emergency trip or a shelf-blocking bulk buy both quietly happen.
steps: Set a clear bin for toilet roll and write a minimum and maximum on the shelf edge.
Sort bulbs into a labeled bin by fitting, and stand batteries upright in a shallow tray by size.
Turn every bin label to face the door.
cards.victory_condition: Every bin carries a minimum and maximum on the shelf edge, and every label faces the door.
cards.source: hand authored, steps grounded in the Manual passes

art.subject: a small dated card fixed to a backstock shelf edge reading a minimum and maximum count, bin labels turned to face forward
must_show: Every bin carries a minimum and maximum on the shelf edge, and every label faces the door.
art.accept_test: The picture shows the finished state the victory condition describes, not the work in progress and not a person doing it.

cards.title: OPEN EVERY LID ON THE FLOOR IN DAYLIGHT
cards.objective: Open every lid on the floor in daylight and name what's actually inside, so nothing unnamed keeps its bin.
cards.why_it_matters: A bin nobody can name without opening it is not storage, it is a decision that keeps getting postponed.
steps: Every lid comes off, on the floor, in daylight. Decorations for a tree you no longer put up, the guest pillow gone flat and yellow, and the bin marked "misc" whose contents you cannot name without looking all go.
For anything you keep, name the occasion in the next twelve months you'll use it.
Reseal only what you named an occasion for.
cards.victory_condition: Every remaining bin can be named without opening it, and nothing inside is flat, yellowed, or for a tradition you no longer keep.

art.subject: several storage bins opened on a closet floor in daylight, their lids set aside while contents are sorted into keep and go piles
must_show: Every remaining bin can be named without opening it, and nothing inside is flat, yellowed, or for a tradition you no longer keep.
art.accept_test: The picture shows the finished state the victory condition describes, not the work in progress and not a person doing it.

cards.title: LABEL EVERY BIN AND MAP THE SHELF
cards.objective: Label each bin with its contents and the month it was last closed, and tape a shelf map inside the door.
cards.why_it_matters: A shelf map means someone else can find the guest bedding without unstacking the whole shelf to look.
steps: Seal guest pillows inside a zip bag.
Label each bin with its contents and the month it was last closed.
Tape a simple shelf map inside the closet door showing which bin sits where.
cards.victory_condition: Every bin is labeled with its contents and last-closed month, and a shelf map is taped inside the door.
cards.source: hand authored, steps grounded in the Manual passes

art.subject: a labeled storage bin standing on a shelf beside a small paper map taped to the inside of a closet door
must_show: Every bin is labeled with its contents and last-closed month, and a shelf map is taped inside the door.
art.accept_test: The picture shows the finished state the victory condition describes, not the work in progress and not a person doing it.

cards.title: THE FULL CLOSET SAFETY AND HEIGHT WALK
cards.objective: Walk every shelf checking what sits above a safe reach, whether a stool actually lives in the closet, and whether bleach and ammonia are kept apart.
cards.why_it_matters: A heavy bin overhead and two chemicals stored together both hide until someone tests for them on purpose.
inputs: a cloth for the awkward spots
steps: Check every shelf for anything a small child could reach that shouldn't be reachable.
Confirm a step stool actually lives inside this closet, not somewhere else in the house.
Confirm bleach and ammonia products sit on separate shelves.
cards.victory_condition: Nothing unsafe sits within a small child's reach, a working stool lives in the closet, and bleach and ammonia sit apart.
cards.source: hand authored, steps grounded in the Manual passes

art.subject: a step stool standing inside an open hall closet beneath a high shelf, bleach and ammonia products visible on separate shelves below it
must_show: Nothing unsafe sits within a small child's reach, a working stool lives in the closet, and bleach and ammonia sit apart.
art.accept_test: The picture shows the finished state the victory condition describes, not the work in progress and not a person doing it.

cards.title: THE WEEKLY GAP-AND-DATE PASS
cards.objective: Walk every bin and shelf reading what's low or undated before the shopping list gets written, and name who is doing it this week.
cards.why_it_matters: Nothing in this closet forces the issue by running out on schedule, so it fails silently unless somebody is actually assigned to look.
steps: Walk the backstock and linen shelves and read the gaps before the list gets written.
Say out loud, or write down, whose turn it is to do this pass this week.
Add anything genuinely missing to the list on the spot.
cards.victory_condition: The shelves were read for gaps before this week's list was written, and one named person did it.
cards.source: hand authored, steps grounded in the Manual passes

art.subject: a hand writing an item onto a shopping list while standing in front of an open hall closet shelf with a visible gap
must_show: The shelves were read for gaps before this week's list was written, and one named person did it.
art.accept_test: The picture shows the finished state the victory condition describes, not the work in progress and not a person doing it.

cards.title: THE MONTHLY LABEL AND LIMIT AUDIT
cards.objective: Once a month, check every written minimum, maximum and date against what's actually on the shelves, and correct any that have drifted.
cards.why_it_matters: A limit written once and never revisited stops meaning anything the first time a good deal tempts you past it.
inputs: this month's receipts if you kept them
steps: Compare the count on each backstock line against its written minimum and maximum.
Check every stored date is still legible and relabel anything faded.
Correct any label that has drifted from what's actually true.
cards.victory_condition: Every limit sits checked this month, and every date on the shelf is legible.
cards.source: hand authored, steps grounded in the Manual passes

art.subject: a hand comparing a shelf's item count against a small dated card fixed to a backstock shelf edge
must_show: Every limit sits checked this month, and every date on the shelf is legible.
art.accept_test: The picture shows the finished state the victory condition describes, not the work in progress and not a person doing it.

cards.title: LINEN SHELF ZONE STANDARD
cards.tagline: WRITE IT. SIGN IT. PUT IT WHERE IT HAPPENS.
cards.objective: Three sets per bed, each nested in its own pillowcase, with the size and count written on the shelf edge.
cards.trigger: When you strip the beds on laundry day, the fresh set comes off this shelf and you read the count as you lift it.
cards.instruction: This is a write on card. Fill it in with a pen, in your own words if the printed sentence is not yours, and put it where the zone is. A standard nobody signed is a preference.
micro_quest: Run a hand along the shelf lip where dust drifts down onto the folded stacks and wipe it clear before it settles onto clean linen.
Check the underside of one shelf bracket for dust that clings and drops onto the stack below it.
Shake out one folded set and refold it to the same width as the rest, catching a musty note before it seals back into the stack.

cards.trigger: When you take the last roll or the last pack of bulbs out of a bin, the restock goes on the shopping list on that same trip to the closet.

cards.title: THE LAST-MINUTE BED CHANGE
cards.objective: A guest is arriving in twenty minutes and the right-sized bed linen has to answer immediately.
cards.held_if: A labeled, complete set for that exact bed size comes off the shelf in one grab, no unfolding others to check.
cards.if_it_failed: If you had to unfold more than one stack to find a set that actually fit, the sizing and labeling slipped. Draw HCA-002.
cards.instruction: Do not do anything to prepare. Live the day, then read the two lines below and be honest about which one you are.
cards.source: hand authored, not in the Manual

art.subject: a hand pulling a labeled, complete sheet set from a linen shelf in one motion, a bed-size card visible on the shelf edge beneath it
must_show: A guest is arriving in twenty minutes and the right-sized bed linen has to answer immediately.
art.accept_test: The pressure has to be visible in the objects. No people's faces, so the load has to be shown by what is on the surfaces and, where unavoidable, by hands and feet alone.

cards.title: THE SPILL THAT NEEDS THE VACUUM NOW
cards.objective: Something breaks in the kitchen and the vacuum has to come out and work, right now, with no time for a fight.
cards.held_if: The vacuum rolls out of its outline, cord already wrapped, every attachment already in its bag.
cards.if_it_failed: If you had to hunt for an attachment or untangle the cord first, the reset after the last use slipped. Draw HCA-004.
cards.instruction: Do not do anything to prepare. Live the day, then read the two lines below and be honest about which one you are.
cards.source: hand authored, not in the Manual

cards.title: THE TODDLER LOOSE IN THE HALLWAY
cards.objective: A toddler gets ten unsupervised seconds near this closet door before anyone notices.
cards.held_if: Nothing on this shelf is within their reach, and nothing unlabeled is within reach either.
cards.if_it_failed: If a bottle was within reach or unlabeled, the height and labeling rules slipped. Draw HCA-006.

cards.title: THE SURPRISE POWER CUT
cards.objective: The power goes out at nine at night and the household needs working batteries, fast, with no time to test three dead ones first.
cards.held_if: The battery tray gives up the right size in one glance, no digging, and it works.
cards.if_it_failed: If the battery you grabbed was already dead or the right size was impossible to find, the sorting and dating slipped. Draw HCA-008.

cards.title: THE UNANNOUNCED OVERNIGHT GUEST
cards.objective: A guest is staying tonight, unannounced, and the guest bedding has to come out of storage in under five minutes.
cards.held_if: The shelf map sends you straight to the right bin, and the pillow inside is sealed, plump and fresh.
cards.if_it_failed: If you had to open two or three bins to find the right one, or the pillow was flat, the labeling and the map slipped. Draw HCA-010.
